claims: The Easter Vigil is held on Holy Saturday night.
The Easter Vigil marks the Resurrection of Jesus.
The Easter Vigil starts in darkness with a service of light.
The Easter Vigil includes the celebration of Baptism/Confirmation for new members.
The Easter Vigil includes the first Eucharist of Easter.
The Service of Light begins after nightfall outside the church.
The Service of Light includes blessing a new fire.
The Service of Light includes lighting the Paschal Candle.
The Service of Light includes singing the Exsultet (Easter Proclamation).
The Liturgy of the Word includes seven Old Testament readings.
The Liturgy of the Word includes two New Testament readings (Epistle and Gospel).
Some readings may be omitted in the Liturgy of the Word.
The Baptismal Liturgy includes the blessing of baptismal water.
The Baptismal Liturgy includes the celebration of baptism.
The Baptismal Liturgy includes the reception of new members into the Church.
The Baptismal Liturgy is followed by the renewal of baptismal promises.
The Liturgy of the Eucharist is the final part of the Easter Vigil Mass.
The Liturgy of the Eucharist celebrates the Eucharist with newly baptized members.
According to a guide by Hallow, the Easter Vigil is not an anticipated Mass for Sunday.
According to a guide by Hallow, the Easter Vigil fulfills the Easter obligation.
According to the USCCB, the Easter Vigil is considered the greatest and most noble of all solemnities.
The Easter Vigil is the "mother of all vigils" in the Catholic Church.
